key_insight: Adding a fixed hard-constraint projection layer to a PINN enforces a local discrete Burgers’ equation constraint and improves accuracy over a comparable PINN.
engineering_relevance: Hard constraint projection could improve physics consistency and reduce sensitivity to collocation-point selection in neural fluid-flow solvers.
method: Locally discretise the nonlinear 1D Burgers’ equation using a finite-difference stencil.
Decompose the discrete equation into constraint and prediction matrices to construct a projection.
Project PINN velocity predictions onto the discrete constraint hyperplane using a non-trainable final layer.
evidence_signal: Initial tests on an unseen uniform grid showed approximately an order-of-magnitude lower data error than a comparable PINN, alongside better governing-equation adherence.
watch_item: Exact enforcement applies to the local discrete constraint, not the continuous PDE; results are preliminary and limited to 1D Burgers’ equation.
paper_title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
